doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

chapter: Jazz life and the state of jazz
title: Demystifying jazz: falling in love with the music
summary: From boogie-woogie at eight to a Horace Silver record at twelve; no jazz teaching in the 1950s.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: You said in around 1990 during one of your presentations, you have a desire to demystify the world of jazz. Jazz musicians are just like the rest of us only more so. Can you expand on that a tad?

Sure. I first fell in love with the music when I was like, well that’s not fair ‘cause when I was really little I liked boogie-woogie and that’s pretty close to jazz. And just the drive and forward momentum of it felt so good when you’re an 8-year-old kid man, I loved that. But when I was like 12 or 13 I heard a Horace Silver record. And it really just stunned me. I thought who are these people? Where are they? How can I find out what they’re doing? What is this thing they’re doing? Because you’ve got to remember back then this would have been in the ‘50s, they didn’t really teach jazz anywhere. And if you wanted to learn it you had to get next to the people and be there. And so it was like learning a foreign language. It was free range. And so I became fascinated with the people who made the music as well as the music.
